overall: Atlanta hit a daily high of 89.6°F at approximately 16:49 ET, and temperatures have been declining steadily for over 5 hours, now sitting at 82.4°F as of 22:10 ET. The day ran notably hotter than anticipated, with the observed peak exceeding all NWP model forecasts by a substantial margin. No precipitation occurred and skies were mostly FEW-SCT during peak heating hours, allowing strong solar forcing.
forecast_obs_notes: All NWP models significantly underforecast today's high — ECMWF came in at 86.6°F, HRRR at 84.9°F, and NBM at 85.1°F, all missing the observed 89.6°F peak by 3.0–4.7°F. The give-up classifier fired at hour 14.87 with 87% confidence the peak was already in, which proved correct as the running max has been locked at 89.6°F since ~17:00 ET.
max_temp_prediction: The daily TMAX of 89.6°F is effectively certain — it was observed at 16:52 ET, the temperature has declined ~7°F since then with no prospect of recovery this late in the evening, and the INTRADAY model assigns 96.8% probability to the 88–89°F bucket that contains 89.6°F. Confidence is extremely high; there is essentially no realistic scenario in which tonight's temperature rebounds to a new daily high. The META model's broader spread into 90–91°F and 92–93°F buckets reflects prior model uncertainty before today's observations locked in.
